_comment: KOREA / Korean template. The answer is shown in REVISED ROMANIZATION (Latin alphabet, green — the phonetics) with the native Korean (Hangul, 한글) on a smaller line BELOW it. Per item: prompt = English shown phrase, answer = romanization revealed in green, native = Hangul shown beneath. The spoken voiceover reads the native Hangul (NOT the romanization). Same Asian-girl character as Japanese, single Korea flag, voice hanabad (default Korean female, native Seoul delivery — round-trip STT verified it reads Hangul naturally) + model eleven_multilingual_v2. Use 9 items per video; keep each romanization answer to ONE line (≤~13 chars) so the two-line answer+Hangul doesn't crowd the 9-row stack — prefer natural short forms (e.g. Annyeong for hi, not the full Annyeonghaseyo). Hangul resolves via Chromium's system-font fallback (no bundled font needed, same as Japanese kana/kanji) — if it ever tofus, bundle Noto Sans KR via fonts[]. Backgrounds: set a Korean bg_query per video; a Pexels miss falls back to the curated versatile-korean pool (so it never pulls a wrong-country image).
outro: Follow me to learn Korean every day
